svg.text: The Retrieval Problem
Goal: Given a query, return the most relevant document chunks
• No single algorithm reliably handles all query types and domain words
• Each algorithm has clear failure modes that other systems compensate for
• Production RAG combines systems to exploit individual performance peaks
Sparse Retrieval: BM25
Dominant keyword algorithm expanding on classic TF-IDF principles
Good at: Exact term matching, unique product IDs, and named entities
Fails at: Vocabulary mismatch ("car" query won't hit "automobile" chunk)
Weakness: Degrades heavily on short 1-2 word ambiguous keyword lookups
Dense Retrieval: What it Handles Well
Embeds queries and documents into a shared continuous vector space
• Semantic matching: Links "session expires" conceptually to "3600 seconds"
• Paraphrase matching: Groups different words sharing identical concepts
• Cross-lingual retrieval: Aligns abstract concepts across global languages
Dense Retrieval: Critical Failure Modes
• Rare/OOV terms: Forces explicit error codes into generic nearest domains
• Exact strings: Conflates highly distinct products (e.g., "GPT-4" vs "GPT-4o")
• High specificity: Blurs targeted queries into wide general theme buckets
• Numbers/Structure: Cannot resolve structured mathematical or date filters
BM25 Formula Mechanics
• IDF component: Drastically penalizes ultra-common grammatical filler words
• TF saturation (k1): Caps the mathematical advantage of high word repetition
• Length norm (b): Shifts preferential scoring weight to shorter documents
Hybrid Retrieval & Fusion
RRF(c) = SUM[ 1 / (k + rank_s(c)) ]
• Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF): Robustly merges dense and sparse rankings
• Rank-driven: Skips complex score normalization entirely to prevent skew
• Weighted Score: alpha * dense + (1 - alpha) * BM25 (prone to scaling artifacts)
Production tip: Fetch large pools (top 50-100) before executing fusion calculations
Query Expansion & Reformulation
Bridges formatting/vocabulary style gaps between users and text bodies
• Synonym expansion: Boosts broad recall terms but risks adding text noise
• Multi-query: LLM spawns alternative phrasings; results are deduplicated
• Step-back prompting: Queries a generalized topic first to gain baseline context
Contextual & Conversational Retrieval
Resolves context-dependent follow-up prompts in multi-turn dialogues
• Standalone query gen: LLM rewrites the query to include implicit context
• Conversation embedding: Directly concatenates recent history into vector
Tradeoff: Standalone gen is far more accurate; context embedding offers lower latency
Knowledge Graph Retrieval (GraphRAG)
Maps complex cross-document dependencies text similarity cannot resolve
• Method: Extracts entities and relations into JSON triplets from chunks
• Execution: Query entities trigger local neighborhood graph traversal
• Integration: Merged directly into text results to enrich background schema
Tradeoff: Excellent for intricate systems (legal/medical); high ingestion overhead
Retrieval Evaluation Metrics
• Recall@k: Primary RAG metric. Fraction of true docs caught in top-k pool
• Precision@k: Density of truly relevant materials inside top-k returns
• MRR: Reciprocal ranking score focusing exclusively on the top hit accuracy
• NDCG: Position-graded valuation penalizing lower placed relevant answers
Rule of thumb: If a chunk misses Recall@k, the LLM cannot recover it
